name: Gonbad-e Qābus
description: Rising from the plains of north-east Iran, Gonbad-e Qābus is a brick tomb tower finished in 1006 for the Ziyarid ruler Qābus Ibn Voshmgir. Its tapering cylinder, topped with a cone-shaped roof, stands about 53 metres high. It is all that survives of the medieval city of Jorjan, a centre of learning, and it inspired tomb towers across Iran, Anatolia and Central Asia.
